subject: Post-demo recap: hosting preference + migration constraints
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Samiha Rahman <samiha@lumaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: hosting preference + migration constraints

Hi Samiha —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Demo highlights (very brief):
- Streaming responses + token-level cost dashboard you asked about
- Canary routing between Hosted / Dedicated with automatic fallback
- KV prefix caching for low-latency multi-turn UX

You mentioned three hosting modes on the call: Hosted API for quick rollout, Dedicated capacity for steady production traffic, and Private VPC for PCI-adjacent flows. To make the recommendation for your team I need two pieces of clarification: 
1) Migration origin: where will the initial traffic be coming from — a third-party LLM API (e.g., other cloud vendor), self-hosted weights in your on-prem clusters, or legacy GPU pools behind a private API?
2) Data residency + connectivity: do you require a VPC peering connection (we can do AWS/GCP/Azure), or will a dedicated VPN and on-prem installation be necessary for the first 6 months?

Proposed immediate next steps (if that works for you):
- Samiha: confirm migration origin (one-line reply is fine) and whether procurement needs a draft SOW/quote to start vendor evaluation (we can send a placeholder).
- Marissa & Karthik: we’ll prepare a short table of recommended mode, expected week-1 latency range, and primary ops asks based on Samiha’s answers.
- I’ll attach the demo recording and a migration checklist for your infra team’s quick review.

Attachments: demo recording, Luma_playbook_requirements_v1.pdf, migration-checklist-template.xlsx

Thanks — I’ll hold off on a full proposal until we confirm the migration origin.

Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
iri@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

---
Redwood Inference — production-first inference for teams
From: Samiha Rahman <samiha@lumaretail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumaRetail Procurement <procurement@lumaretail.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: hosting preference + migration constraints

Hi Irene —

Thanks for the recap and the recording — looks good. Short answers below: 

1) Migration origin: majority of traffic will be migrating from a mix — we currently use a commercial LLM API for customer-facing chat (75% of queries). The rest (25%) runs on an internal GPU pool (legacy Kubernetes nodes) that hosts a small LLM for internal tooling. The commercial API is the primary concern for credentials/contract overlap.

2) Data residency / connectivity: for now we want Hosted API for non-PII interactions, but any flows that touch payment tokens or PII must go Private (VPC or dedicated on-prem). We would likely pilot on Hosted for 6–8 weeks and then move higher-risk flows to Private. We are open to Dedicated if it simplifies the handoff.

Procurement: yes please send a placeholder SOW/quote; we’ll share it with our legal and procurement teams.

Samiha Rahman
Head of Platform Integrations, LumaRetail
samiha@lumaretail.com | +1 (617) 555-2281

On a related note, do you have an estimate for the amount of work to migrate the KV-indexed chat context from our legacy Kubernetes service into Redwood’s prefix cache? Our infra lead asked for a rough effort estimate to budget for engineering time.
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: LumaRetail migration questions + ops checklist

Internal note (do not forward as-is) —

Quick breakdown and proposed owner map: 
- Migration origin mix: 75% commercial API, 25% legacy k8s GPU pool. This means we should plan for: token accounting reconciliation (commercial API vs Redwood hosted), credential rotation policy for cutover, and a two-phase migration plan (pilot Hosted for low-risk; then Dedicated/Private for PII flows).

- KV prefix cache migration: estimate 2–3 engineering sprints from Luma infra + 1 sprint from our side (SE support + migration scripts). Key unknown: the format of the existing KV store and whether they persist embeddings or raw text. Ask Samiha to share a short sample export (anonymized).

Action items: 
1) Marissa: prepare a placeholder SOW and a pricing sketch with three options (Hosted-only pilot, Dedicated reserve w/ hybrid fallback, Private VPC deployment) — include 30/60/90 day rollout costs. Target to have this by Wednesday EOD.
2) Rishi: draft a short migration playbook section on credential rotation and canary cutover steps (include rollback plan).
3) Irene: request the sample KV export from Samiha and confirm procurement contact.

I’ll attach a lightweight ops checklist template we've used on similar customers.

Thanks,
Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Samiha Rahman <samiha@lumaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, LumaRetail Procurement <procurement@lumaretail.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: hosting preference + migration constraints

Hi Samiha —

Perfect, thanks for the clear answers. Two quick clarifications and then next steps from us: 

Clarifications: 
- KV export: an anonymized sample JSON or CSV (a handful of rows) is sufficient — we don’t need anything production. This lets Karthik validate the schema and confirm the 2–3 sprint estimate.
- Pilot scope: for the Hosted pilot we recommend starting with the top 3 non-PII intents (customer chat + returns triage + pricing lookup). That should keep the risk low while giving us meaningful traffic for cost/latency calculations.

Next steps we’ll take this week: 
- Marissa will send a placeholder SOW/quote with three hosting scenarios (target: Wed EOD).
- Karthik will attach the ops checklist and an initial migration playbook excerpt for credential rotation by Wed.
- I’ll loop in our Security Engineering lead if you want early alignment on Private VPC requirements; otherwise we can wait until the pilot results.

Could you share the KV export and the procurement contact name/email by EOD tomorrow so Marissa can route the SOW? If it helps, I can drop a short template procurement email you can forward.

Thanks again — excited to get this moving.

Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
iri@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments included: migration-checklist-template.xlsx
